rationale: Lycopolitan plural of ⲙⲟⲩ 'water.' Used in the cosmological phrase 'ship of the living waters' (ⲡⲧⲭⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲙⲙⲟⲩⲉⲩⲉ ⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ̄), referring to the Living Waters of Manichaean cosmology — the third Living Element which the First Man wears as armor and which is borne by the cosmic ship.
Lycopolitan reflex of ϩⲱⲃⲥ̄/ϩⲗⲱⲃϣ̄ 'cover, garment.' Context (line 31, paired with 'in his...') suggests an item of clothing or covering associated with Death.
Triple-form doxological closure formula: ϣⲁ-ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ ('unto eternity') + ⲛⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ ('and ever') + ⲛ-ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ ('of ages'). Lycopolitan ⲁⲛⲏⲍⲉ = Sahidic ⲉⲛⲉϩ. Marks chapter end.
